Interface IuDao

public interface IuDao
Data-access facade over a single DataSource, providing generated SQL for JPA-annotated entities alongside ad-hoc JDBC operations.

Obtain an instance from of(DataSource, TransactionManager, TransactionSynchronizationRegistry). Entity mapping is driven by the annotations described on IuSqlBuilder, so an entity needs @Table plus @Column or @SqlColumn getters. An entity type may be a class with a no-argument constructor, which is instantiated and populated through its setters, or an interface, which is materialized as an immutable view of the row it was read from.

Methods fall into two families. The get* family returns an unexecuted ParameterizedSql the caller drives and closes; see that interface for which accessors close themselves. The remaining methods — loadBean(Class, Map), searchBeans(Class, Map), updateBean(Object), saveBean(Object), deleteBean(Object), and the bulk variants — execute immediately and leave no resources open.

A DAO holds no per-call state and may be shared between threads. Reads performed by loadBean(Class, Map) and searchBeans(Class, Map, boolean, int) are cached, but only for the duration of an active transaction and only in that transaction's own TransactionSynchronizationRegistry resources, so cached rows can never outlive the transaction that read them or leak across threads. Writes through this facade evict the affected entity type; direct SQL does not, so call clear() after modifying rows by other means.

    • getBeanUpdate

      SqlStatement getBeanUpdate(Object bean, Supplier<?> passive)
      Gets an unexecuted delta update covering only the columns whose values differ from the entity as originally read.

      passive is invoked at most once, and only if a comparison is actually needed, so callers may supply an original that is itself expensive to load.

      Parameters:
      bean - entity carrying both the new values and the key to match
      passive - supplies the entity's original state; when null, or when it supplies null, every mapped non-key column is updated
      Returns:
      unexecuted update statement
      Throws:
      IuSqlUnchangedException - if no mapped column differs from the original
      NullPointerException - if bean is null

    • updateBean

      void updateBean(Object bean)
      Updates the row matching an entity's key and evicts that entity type from the transaction-scoped cache.

      An entity whose mapped columns all match the database is left alone rather than reported as an error.

      An EffectiveDated entity is not modified in place: a new row superseding its current one is inserted instead, carrying the changed values and copying the rest. Nothing matching the entity's key means there is no row to supersede, which is reported as an error the same way it is for an ordinary entity.

      Parameters:
      bean - entity carrying both the new values and the key to match
      Throws:
      jakarta.persistence.EntityNotFoundException - if no row matches the entity's key
      jakarta.persistence.NonUniqueResultException - if more than one row was updated
      NullPointerException - if bean is null

    • getQuery

      <B> SqlQuery<B> getQuery(Class<B> beanClass, String sql, Iterable<?> args)
      Gets an unexecuted query over caller-supplied SQL and its bind arguments, materializing each row by matching result-set column labels to the target type's properties.

      A mapped entity's labels are resolved through its @Column and @SqlColumn mappings; any label that resolves to no mapped property, and every label of an unmapped type, falls back to matching the property name ignoring case and underscores. Labels matching no property are ignored.

      A value is read as the type its column stores and converted to the type its member declares, reversing what IuSqlBuilder.getForSql(Object, String) does when binding the same member: a character column mapped to a boolean reads back "Y" as true, a timestamp column mapped to an Instant reads back as an Instant, and the single space standing in for null on a SpaceForNull column reads back as null. A member belonging to no mapped column is read as its own type.

      A class is instantiated through its no-argument constructor and populated through its setters, skipping values that would assign null to a primitive property. An interface is instead materialized as an immutable view of the row's resolved values: its getters return those values, getters for columns the query did not select return null or the appropriate primitive default, its default methods run as written, and any other abstract method throws UnsupportedOperationException. Such a view stays valid after the query is closed.

      Type Parameters:
      B - result type
      Parameters:
      beanClass - type to materialize, which need not be a mapped entity
      sql - SQL text to execute
      args - bind arguments in placeholder order; may be null or empty
      Returns:
      unexecuted query
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if beanClass is a class that cannot be instantiated, thrown when a row is materialized

      Returns:
      unexecuted query

    • clear

      void clear()
      Discards every cached read for the active transaction, so that subsequent loads and searches go to the database.

      Does nothing when no transaction is active, since nothing is cached outside a transaction.

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the transaction status cannot be determined

    • insertBeans

      void insertBeans(Iterable<?> beans)
      Inserts each entity in turn, then discards every cached read for the active transaction.

      The entities are not inserted atomically: on failure the entities already inserted stay inserted unless an enclosing transaction rolls them back.

      Parameters:
      beans - entities to insert, which need not share a type
      Throws:
      jakarta.persistence.EntityNotFoundException - if an insert affects no row
      jakarta.persistence.NonUniqueResultException - if an insert affects more than one row

    • updateBeans

      void updateBeans(Iterable<?> beans)
      Updates each entity in turn, as if by updateBean(Object).

      The entities are not updated atomically: on failure the entities already updated stay updated unless an enclosing transaction rolls them back.

      Parameters:
      beans - entities to update, which need not share a type
      Throws:
      jakarta.persistence.EntityNotFoundException - if no row matches an entity's key
      jakarta.persistence.NonUniqueResultException - if an update affects more than one row
